Class HttpClient

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.api.io.net.HttpClient
public final class HttpClient extends Object
A minimal HTTP/1.1 client recognized as compiler intrinsics by Juno, backed by the Arduino WiFiS3 library's WiFiClient. Requires @Board(ArduinoUnoR4WiFi.class) (the default board) and an active Wifi.begin(String, String) connection.

host/path (and body for post(String, int, String, String, byte[], int, byte[], int, int[]), patch(String, int, String, String, byte[], int, byte[], int, int[]), and query(String, int, String, String, byte[], int, byte[], int, int[])) must each be a compile-time constant: either a string literal, or System.getenv("NAME") of a literal environment-variable name, exactly like Wifi.begin(String, String)'s credentials. Juno has no heap, so none of these can be a runtime-computed String — this also means these methods must be called directly with the literal in hand, never forwarded through another method's own String parameter.

The response body is written into bodyBuffer and the raw response headers into headersBuffer (both caller-owned, fixed-size byte[]), each starting at index 0 and truncated to its own length if longer — pass each buffer's own array length explicitly, since Juno has no runtime .length for an array method parameter. Each method returns the number of body bytes written, or -1 if the connection failed. statusAndHeadersLength (a caller-owned int[2], allocated once outside any loop like the buffers themselves) is filled with the HTTP status code at index 0 (or 0 if the connection failed before a status line was received) and the number of bytes written into headersBuffer at index 1. Copy these, together with the returned body length, into an HttpResponse for a more convenient caller-owned holder. A request that doesn't complete within a fixed 5-second timeout is abandoned and returns whatever was captured so far.
